nodes.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k$, this property holds when, for any finite groups $G_0, \dots, G_k$ (not necessarily distinct) whose spectra $\pi_e(G_i)$ (the sets of orders of elements of $G_i$) all equal $\Gamma$, there are indices $i \ne j$ with $G_i \cong G_j$.
nodes.title: At most $k$ isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ is the set of orders of elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order counts as having order $0$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a group (Kourovka 13.63)

nodes.summary: The spectrum of a group $G$ is the set $\{\operatorname{ord}(g) : g \in G\}$ of the orders of its elements, where an element of infinite order is counted as having order $0$.
nodes.title: The spectrum of a group (Kourovka 12.84)

nodes.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers, this property holds when, for every natural number $n$, there are $n$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups $G_0, \dots, G_{n-1}$ whose spectra $\pi_e(G_i)$ (the sets of orders of elements of $G_i$) all equal $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$

nodes.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers, let $h(\Gamma)$ be the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups $G$ whose spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ (set of element orders) is $\Gamma$; $h(\Gamma) \le k$ means that among any $k + 1$ finite groups with spectrum $\Gamma$ two are isomorphic, and $h(\Gamma) = \infty$ means that for every $n$ there are $n$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups with spectrum $\Gamma$. nodes.title: No uniform bound on the number of groups with a given spectrum

nodes.summary: The proposition, asked about by W. J. Shi, that there is a natural number $k$ such that for every set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers, either $h(\Gamma) \le k$ or $h(\Gamma) = \infty$, where $h(\Gamma)$ is the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups $G$ whose spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ (set of element orders) is $\Gamma$. nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.63 (bounded or infinite number of groups per spectrum)

nodes.summary: There are a set $\Omega$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k$ such that two non-isomorphic finite groups have set of element orders $\Omega$, but there are no $k$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups whose set of element orders is $\Omega$.
nodes.title: Two isospectral finite groups do not force infinitely many

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every set $\Omega$ of natural numbers, if two non-isomorphic finite groups both have set of element orders $\Omega$, then for every natural number $k$ there are $k$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups whose set of element orders is $\Omega$; that is, infinitely many.
nodes.title: Syskin's question on groups with a given spectrum (Kourovka 12.84)
